name: Fixed-Point Converter
blurb: a decimal value in a Q format and the precision lost
intro: Converts a decimal value to a Q-format integer (or a stored integer back to its value) for any word length and number of fraction bits, with the rounding error, resolution and range. Formats are named both ways: TI Qm.n (m without the sign bit) and ARM Qm.n (m with it).
usage: Give direction = toq with a decimal value, or fromq with the stored integer (decimal or 0x hex bit pattern); plus signed (signed|unsigned), word length in bits, fraction bits, and for toq the rounding (nearest|even|floor|trunc) and overflow (saturate|wrap). Returns the Q name in TI and ARM notation, the stored integer and its hex, the value it represents, the error in absolute, relative and LSB terms, resolution and range, the value in common Q formats, and C macros. Use it to pick a Q format or check a DSP coefficient.
sources: Texas Instruments, TMS320C64x DSP Library Programmer's Reference (SPRU565), Q format notation
ARM CMSIS-DSP documentation, q7_t / q15_t / q31_t types
Wikipedia, Q (number format): TI and ARM notation
